name: T gate by catalysis with a CS gate
summary: A CNOT followed by a controlled-S gate, acting on a qubit and a |T⟩ state, applies a T gate to the qubit and returns the |T⟩ state unchanged.
description:
Using a single copy of the magic state $\ket{T} = \ket{0}+e^{i\pi/4}\ket{1}$ as a *catalyst*, a T gate can be implemented with Clifford gates and one controlled-S (CS) gate: apply a CNOT from the qubit to the catalyst, followed by CS. Here the CS gate $=\mathrm{CZ}(\frac\pi2)$ is written in its standard decomposition into two CNOTs, a $-\frac\pi4$ phase on the target and $\frac\pi4$ phases on both qubits. The two adjacent CNOTs cancel, the $-\frac\pi4$ phase turns the catalyst into $\ket{+}$, which the last CNOT leaves unchanged, and the final $\frac\pi4$ phases apply a T gate to the qubit and restore the catalyst.

Because the catalyst is returned unchanged, one $\ket{T}$ state suffices to replace every T gate of a Clifford+T circuit by a Clifford+CS circuit. Kissinger, Ross and van de Wetering use this kind of catalysis to build complete axiomatisations from the phase-free ZH-calculus by adjoining catalysis rules.
